clue.text: Drink with discontented international broadcaster

indicators.note: content is what fills a thing, so discontented means the inner letters of the preceding word are emptied out

parts.note: the word with with its middle letters removed
I is the standard abbreviation for international
Sky is a British satellite broadcaster

explanation.surface: A drink is taken alongside some disgruntled overseas radio or TV presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discontented' reads as an unhappy mood for the broadcaster, but it works on the little word 'with'. Sky is the UK satellite TV company.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky is a distilled spirit, a common example of an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Fellow employee Mark two interns essentially replaced

indicators.note: replaced means put back in different places, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letter is used

parts.note: the central letter of this seven-letter word

explanation.surface: An employee named Mark has seen two of the interns replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: A workmate is a colleague, someone employed alongside you.

clue.text: During class advanced student becomes relaxed

parts.note: in, as in 'in the night', means during
a form is a school class
A is short for advanced
L is the learner plate letter

explanation.surface: In lessons, a top pupil chills out.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is a school year group in Britain; L stands for learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal means casual or unceremonious, so relaxed in manner.

clue.text: Was familiar with novel being broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than seen, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: novel means new

explanation.surface: Someone recognised a book being read on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' tempts as a book, but here it is the adjective meaning fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Knew is the past tense of know, which means to be acquainted with.

clue.text: Strong fishing nets catching Atlantic tuna primarily about

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the whole assembled string is read the other way
something that catches another thing holds it inside itself

parts.note: trawls are large bag-shaped nets dragged by fishing boats

indicators.note: primarily points to the leading letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Robust nets that scoop up tuna in the Atlantic, lying around on a quay.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAWLS holding AT gives TRAWLATS, which read backwards is STALWART.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalwart describes someone sturdy and dependable, a synonym of strong in build or loyalty.

clue.text: Single-minded determination that Stonehenge road planners had?

parts.note: surface reading: a narrow, obsessive focus on one goal
the setter's reading: the long-debated plan to put the road past Stonehenge underground

explanation.walkthrough: The A303 past Stonehenge, the prehistoric stone circle in Wiltshire, has long had a plan to bury the road in a bore beneath the site; the planners' vision literally involved going underground.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a narrow focus on one goal that ignores everything else.

clue.text: Metal star

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the heavy grey element Pb
second meaning: the principal performer in a show

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it suggests a heavy-metal rock star, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: One spelling serves as the name of a soft heavy element and as the main role in a play or film.

clue.text: Bishop leaves Welsh city, area that produces wool

indicators.note: when someone leaves a place they go out of it, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
Bangor is a cathedral city in north Wales
A is short for area

explanation.surface: A bishop departs from a Welsh cathedral city in a sheep-farming district.
explanation.definitionFit: Angora is a soft yarn made from the hair of Angora goats or rabbits, a type of wool.

clue.text: Fare for 17 Across to get to holiday destination

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the bird traditionally served at the holiday feast in that answer
second meaning: a country popular with sun-seeking tourists

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' looks like a ticket price for a journey, but here it means food.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is the centrepiece of the American harvest-festival dinner, and the same word names the Mediterranean country.

clue.text: Law match official previously bent

indicators.note: previously says the second named item comes before the first in the final order

parts.note: ref is short for referee
lex is Latin for law, familiar from legal phrases

explanation.surface: A referee who once bent the rules of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names the law first, but 'previously' puts the official ahead of it. Bent here is the botanical sense of bent back.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflex, as an adjective, means bent or turned backwards, as in a reflex angle or a reflexed petal.

clue.text: Jeopardise close to ten grand earned building houses

indicators.note: to house something is to give it room inside, so one piece sits within the other
building suggests putting something together from parts into a new form

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter of the following word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word
G is short for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Risking nearly ten thousand pounds earned on a building project that includes houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building houses' reads as a construction project; in fact one word is the anagram signal and the other the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger something is to put it at risk, a direct synonym of jeopardise.

clue.text: Olympian raising the bar?

parts.note: surface reading: an athlete setting a new, higher standard
the setter's reading: literally hoisting a loaded barbell above the head

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'raising the bar' means improving standards; here a bar is lifted for real.
explanation.definitionFit: This Olympic athlete competes by lifting a heavily loaded bar off the ground.

clue.text: Swimmer enjoys going around lake

indicators.note: the words going around something wrap it, so the answer lies inside the run of letters

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A swimmer likes doing laps of the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a lake or pond, a word mostly found in English place names.

clue.text: Reportedly destined to be honoured

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is judged by sound rather than spelling

parts.note: fated means destined; in many accents the two words sound alike

explanation.surface: Supposedly someone's fate is to receive honours.
explanation.definitionFit: To be feted is to be celebrated or lavishly entertained, a synonym of being honoured.

clue.text: Short female cut cheese

indicators.note: to cut something is to remove it, so the named letter is taken away

parts.note: brief means short
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A small woman slices some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short female' looks like a description of a person, but short is the word to be cut and female the letter removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cheese with a white rind.

clue.text: Avoid confronting flipping cheats, caught out

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it the other way round
out means removed, so this letter no longer appears

parts.note: tricks are cheats or deceptions
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone dodges facing up to the blasted cheats who were caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British expletive, but it signals turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirt an issue is to go around its edge rather than deal with it directly.

clue.text: Steal small article Barbie's boyfriend's carrying around

parts.note: S is short for small

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the combined letters run backwards
a person carrying something holds it, so one item sits within the other

parts.note: Ken is the doll who partners Barbie
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Ken is lugging a little item around for Barbie.
explanation.definitionFit: To sneak, like to steal, can mean to move furtively or to take something slyly.

clue.text: Time I missed potentially having skiing holiday

indicators.note: potentially suggests what the letters could become once rearranged
something missed is left out, so one letter drops from the collection

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written, the letter to be removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone missed their time slot on a ski trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is T plus 'having skiing' with one I dropped; this time 'having' is part of the fodder, not a link. Thanksgiving is the American and Canadian harvest holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Thanksgiving is a national public holiday in the US and Canada, celebrated with a family feast.

clue.text: Left relative sandwiches at home

indicators.note: to sandwich something is to place it between two outer layers

parts.note: a sister is a family relative
in means at home

explanation.surface: A relative left some sandwiches at the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Sinister is Latin for left, and in heraldry it still means the left-hand side.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry, sinister denotes the left side of a shield as seen by the bearer.

clue.text: Concern for profit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stake or involvement in something
second meaning: money earned on savings or a loan

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a business worried only about making money; the two nouns are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a share or stake in something and the return paid on money lent.

clue.text: Rubbish inside quiet eastern railway terminus causes outcry

indicators.note: inside places the first item within the letters that follow

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
rot means nonsense
E is short for eastern
a terminus is the end station of a line

explanation.surface: Litter left in a sleepy station at the end of the eastern line sparks complaints.
explanation.definitionFit: A protestation is a strong declaration of objection, so an outcry against something.

clue.text: Doctor is visiting again, he's a saint

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone's home, so one item sits within the other

parts.note: anew means again
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A physician calls round once more, and is hailed as saintly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' wants to be an anagram signal, but it is simply DR.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew the apostle is a saint, patron saint of Scotland.

clue.text: Greek character given occasionally less plain breakfast food

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is taken

parts.note: the even-placed letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A Greek gets a breakfast that is less dull than usual.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a cereal mix of oats, nuts and dried fruit eaten in the morning.

clue.text: Know Musk ignoring all outsiders shows common sense

indicators.note: dropping every outside letter leaves only the middles of the words

parts.note: the inner letters of the word
the inner letters of the name

explanation.surface: A jibe that a famous billionaire shuns outsiders yet displays good judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is an informal British word for practical intelligence, i.e. good common sense.

clue.text: Turn towards celebrity making comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the letters go back the way they came

parts.note: towards means to
a VIP is a very important person

explanation.surface: Fans turn their attention to a star who is staging a return.
explanation.definitionFit: To pivot is to rotate on a fixed point, so it means turn.

clue.text: Fruit, not round as it happens

indicators.note: not tells us the following item is left out of the word

parts.note: an olive is a fruit
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A fruit that, as it happens, isn't round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As it happens' reads as a throwaway phrase, but it is the definition: a live broadcast goes out as events happen.
explanation.definitionFit: A live broadcast is transmitted in real time, while events unfold.

clue.text: Sell VW car in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: the Golf is a Volkswagen hatchback model

explanation.surface: A pensioner sells off their Volkswagen.
explanation.walkthrough: Flog is British slang for sell.
explanation.definitionFit: Flog is informal British slang meaning to sell something, often cheaply.

clue.text: How's it going in France making wine?

wordplay.note: ça va is the everyday French greeting meaning how's it going

explanation.surface: A French greeting over a glass of sparkling wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The cedilla and space are dropped from the French phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Cava is a Spanish sparkling wine, chiefly from Catalonia.

clue.text: Determined to use our steel abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A firm resolve to put national steel to work overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolute describes someone firmly set on a purpose, a synonym of determined.

clue.text: Lowers belt, tactfully turning clasps

indicators.note: turning round means the hidden run is read from right to left
to clasp is to hold, so the words hold the answer within their letters

parts.note: the run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone discreetly lets out a belt by turning its buckle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowers' looks like a verb about dropping a belt; it is a noun, things that low, as cows do.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle low, that is moo, so they are literally lowers in the crossword sense.

clue.text: Those moaning seeing footballers tackling hard

indicators.note: to tackle something is to take it on, here taken in among the letters

parts.note: wingers play on the flanks of a football team
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Players complain after seeing team-mates tackle roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: To whinge is British slang for complaining peevishly, so whingers are moaners.

clue.text: Mimic perhaps Henry's wife books

parts.note: Catherine Parr was the sixth wife of Henry VIII
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Someone imitates the reading tastes of a Tudor queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the definition as an example: a parrot is one kind of mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: A parrot is a bird famous for copying human speech, an example of a mimic.
